122276.subject: Botany
122276.text: How do Aves maintain a constant body temperature?

122276.sol: The main characteristic feature of Aves (birds) is the presence of feathers. Aves are warm-blooded animals, also known as homoiothermous, which means they are able to maintain a constant body temperature. Mammals have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running,climbing, burrowing, swimming or flyingThe most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished. 122915.subject: Botany
122915.text: Aestivation Types Descriptions A. Valvate 1. Sepals or petals overlap each other but not in a particular direction B. Twisted 2. Sepals or petals just touch each other at the margin without overlapping C. Imbricate 3. Largest petal overlaps lateral petals, which overlap the smallest anterior petals D. Vexillary 4. One margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one
122915.sol: Valvate aestivation has sepals or petals just touching each other at the margin without overlapping. Twisted aestivation has margins overlapping one another. Imbricate aestivation involves overlapping in no particular direction, and vexillary (or papilionaceous) involves a specific overlapping pattern of petals

123366.subject: Botany
123366.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1.The mesophyll is composed of palisade and spongy parenchyma. 2.The palisade parenchyma is located below the spongy parenchyma. 3.The spongy parenchyma has large spaces and air cavities between cells. 4.The mesophyll carries out photosynthesis. 5.The spongy parenchyma is arranged vertically and parallel to each other.
123366.sol: Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma,There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells," the palisade parenchyma is located above the spongy parenchyma, and the palisade parenchyma, not the spongy parenchyma, is arranged vertically.

124515.subject: Botany
124515.text: What role does oxygen play in plant growth?
options: It releases metabolic energy essential for growth activities
124515.sol: The plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement which in turn requires water. Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth. Thus, plant growth and further development is intimately linked to the water status of the plant. Water also provides the medium for enzymatic activities needed for growth. Oxygen helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities.

124580.subject: Botany
124580.text: Which compound is not naturally occurring but has cell division promoting activity?
124580.sol: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Cytokinins have specific effects on cytokinesis, and were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA. Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants

124635.subject: Botany

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
124635.sol: Quantitative comparisons between the growth of living system can also be made in two ways : (i) measurement and the comparison of total growth per unit time is called the absolute growth rate. (ii) The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, e.g., per unit initial parameter is called the relative growth rate.

124655.subject: Botany
124655.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Ethylene delays fruit ripening Reason: It reduces the respiration rate of during ripening of fruits
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
124655.sol: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of the fruits.

124913.subject: Botany
124913.text: What are the compounds that are oxidized during respiration known as?
124913.sol: Photosynthesis, of course, takes place within the chloroplasts (in the eukaryotes), whereas the breakdown of complex molecules to yield energy takes place in the cytoplasm and in the mitochondria (also only in eukaryotes). The breaking of the C-C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to release of considerable amount of energy is called respiration. The compounds that are oxidized during this process are known as respiratory substrates. Usually carbohydrates are oxidized to release

125267.subject: Botany
125267.text: Azolla is used as a biofertilizer because it
options: multiplies very fast to produce massive biomass
has association of nitrogen - fixing Rhizobium
has association of nitrogen - fixing cyan obacteria
125267.sol: Azolla is a pteridophyte and used as a biofertilizer because it has association with nitrogenfixing cyanobacteria Anabaena azollae.

125690.subject: Botany
125690.text: Assertion : CAM plants lack structural compartmentation of leaf as found in C ₄ plants. Reason : Stomata of CAM plants are open during the day.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
125690.sol: CAM plants do not exhibit the structural compartmentation as shown by C ₄ plants which exhibit kranz anatomy. CAM plants fix CO ₂ at night because their stomata are open at night and remain closed during the day.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

126273.subject: Botany
126273.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The pollen tube enters the embryo sac through the micropylar end into one of the synergids. Reason (R): The filiform apparatus present at the micropylar tip of the egg cell guides the entry of the pollen tube. Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
126273.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because during fertilization in angiosperms, the pollen tube typically enters the embryo sac at the micropylar end and penetrates into one of the synergids. Reason (R) is incorrect because the filiform apparatus is present at the micropylar tip of the synergids, not the egg cell. 127258.subject: Botany
127258.text: Find the correct sequence among the following
127258.sol: angiosperm being the maximum in number followed by the fungi further followed by the algae after which comes up with mosses, fern and lichens being the lowest in the number.

127268.subject: Botany
127268.text: David Tilman's long term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots showed that:
options: Plots with more species showed less year to year variation in total biomas
Increased diversity contributed to higher productivity.
127268.sol: We don’t know how these attributes are linked to species richness in a community, but David Tilman’s long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots provide some tentative answers. Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass. He also showed that in his experiments, increased diversity contributed to higher productivity.

127467.subject: Botany
127467.text: Which of the following is the most important cause for animals and plants being driven to extinction?
127467.sol: From the evil quartet, habitat loss and fragmentation due to over population, urbanization and industrialization is the major cause of extinction. Loss of habitat and fragmentation endangers the survival of wildlife species by exposing them to a higher degree of pollution. Tropical rainforests, previously covering an area of 14%, have been reduced to 6% in recent times. This has led to the extinction of several species over the last few centuries.

127730.subject: Botany
127730.text: Ecosystem Function Definition A. Productivity 1. Unidirectional flow of energy B. Decomposition 2. Breaking down of dead organic matter C. Energy Flow 3. Conversion of inorganic to organic matter by autotrophs D. Nutrient Cycling 4. Reuse of nutrients through decomposition
127730.sol: Productivity (A) refers to the conversion of inorganic to organic matter by autotrophs (3). Decomposition (B) is the breaking down of dead organic matter (2). Energy Flow (C) is the unidirectional flow of energy (1). Nutrient Cycling (D) involves the reuse of nutrients through decomposition (4).

128943.subject: Zoology
128943.text: What is the other term for Coronary Artery Disease?
128943.sol: Coronary Artery Disease, often referred to as atherosclerosis , affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle. It is caused by deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissues, which makes the lumen of arteries narrower.

129067.subject: Zoology
129067.text: To obtain a standard electrocardiogram (ECG) for continuously monitoring basic heart activity, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads. What is the correct anatomical placement of these three leads?
options: One to each wrist and one to the left ankle
One to each ankle and one to the left wrist
One to the right wrist and one to the left ankle
Multiple leads attached only to the chest region
129067.sol: To obtain a standard ECG, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads: one to each wrist and one to the left ankle. This configuration continuously monitors the basic heart activity. For a more detailed evaluation of the heart's function, multiple leads are attached to the chest region, but the standard baseline setup requires only the three specific limb leads. Swapping the placement (e.g., each ankle and left wrist) or missing a lead is incorrect. Answer: One to each wrist and one to the lef

129622.subject: Zoology
129622.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Cortical nephron has short loop of Henle 2. Peritubular capillaries are formed by afferent arteriole 3. PCT open into collecting ducts 4. A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb 5. The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called collecting duct
129622.sol: In majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla. A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the next part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb. The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted tubule (DCT). The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called collecting duct.

130563.subject: Zoology
130563.text: What qualities should an ideal contraceptive have?
options: User-friendly, easily available, effective, and reversible with no or least side-effects
130563.sol: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible with no or least side-effects. It also should in no way interfere with the sexual drive, desire and/or the sexual act of the user . A wide range of contraceptive methods are presently available which could be broadly grouped into the following categories, namely Natural/Traditional, Barrier, IUDs, Oral contraceptives, Injectables, Implants and Surgical methods.

130668.subject: Zoology
130668.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: World population rocketed from 2 billion in 1900 to 7.2 billion in 2011 Reason: In the last century an all-round development in various fields significantly improved the quality of life of the people.

130668.sol: Increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of population. The world population which was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 rocketed to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011.

130864.subject: Zoology
130864.text: What is the function of the clitoris in the female external genitalia?

A cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair
To lie at the upper junction of the two labia minora

The labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue, which extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening. The labia minora are paired folds of tissue under the labia majora. 131181.subject: Zoology
131181.text: Which of the following hormones is not secreted by human placenta?
131181.sol: Placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, progestogens, etc. LH is secreted by pituitary gland.

131442.subject: Zoology
131442.text: When was the discovery of nuclein made?
options: At the same time as the proposition of principles of inheritance by Mendel
Before the discovery of the principles of inheritance by Mendel
After the discovery of the principles of inheritance by Mendel
131442.sol: Even though the discovery of nuclei by Meischer and the proposition for principles of inheritance by Mendel were almost at the same time , the fact that DNA acts as a genetic material took a long time to be discovered and proven. By 1926, the quest to determine the mechanism for genetic inheritance had reached the molecular level. Previous discoveries by Gregor Mendel, Walter Sutton, Thomas Hunt Morgan and numerous other scientists had narrowed the search to the chromosomes located in the nucleus of most cells. But

131731.subject: Zoology
131731.text: Codon Characteristic Function A. UUU 1. Codes for Phenylalanine B. AUG 2. Acts as an initiator codon and codes for Methionine C. UAA, UAG, UGA 3. Function as stop codons D. Codon Redundancy 4. Code for different amino acids in different organisms
131731.sol: A - 1: UUU codes for Phenylalanine. B - 2: AUG acts as an initiator codon and also codes for Methionine. C - 3: UAA, UAG, and UGA function as stop codons. D - 4: Codon redundancy means that some codons can code for the same amino acid.

131734.subject: Zoology
131734.text: Level Description A. Transcriptional Level 1. Regulation of mRNA splicing B. Processing Level 2. Regulation of mRNA transport from nucleus to cytoplasm C. Transport Level 3. D - 4: Translational Level involves the control of protein synthesis after mRNA is translated.

131778.subject: Zoology

131778.sol: When the small subunit encounters an mRNA, the process of translation of the mRNA to protein begins.

prophase in cell of female mammal
prophase in cell of male mammal.

134085.subject: Zoology
